arc-ink.note: The only brand value that moves between themes, because text is the one place it has to.

sky.note: Atmosphere only. Unpaired in the tokens: nothing may put text on it.

ink-3.note: The lowest step that may carry text.

ink-4.note: Not text. Disabled glyphs, gridlines, scrollbar thumb.

mesh-ink.note: Ink for dark grounds. Pinned in both themes.

person-ink.note: Pinned ink on all six identity fields.

2xs.purpose: A count in a badge, a tick on an axis. Never prose.

xs.purpose: Column heads, timestamps, units, pager text, the quiet half of a two-line cell.

sm.purpose: Dense rows, chips, menu items, buttons, inputs — anything in a list the eye runs down.

base.purpose: The default: body, rail and panel labels, the line of a row that carries the record.

md.purpose: One sentence under a title. The largest size still set at 400.

lg.purpose: A page title, a dialog title, a section heading inside a modal.

xl.purpose: A plate heading. One per screen.

2xl.purpose: A modal's title, and the label beside a screen figure.

3xl.purpose: A screen's figure, where the screen has one.

4xl.purpose: Between the figure and the monument.

5xl.purpose: The monumental figure. One shipped use, on the dashboard.

figure.purpose: The `figure` utility: display face at 88% width, tabular lining numerals, 0.82 line-height. The monumental figure and plate numbers, nowhere else.

shadows.name: hairline
shadows.purpose: The one line this system draws: a data boundary. Inset, so it costs no layout and follows any radius.

shadows.name: field-edge
shadows.purpose: The lip of a filled well — inputs, selects, the outline button.

shadows.name: panel
shadows.purpose: A panel: paper on glacier, held by an edge rather than lifted by a shadow. No drop shadow.

shadows.name: panel-raised
shadows.value: inset 0 0 0 1px color-mix(in oklch, var(--ink) 9%, transparent), 0 2px 6px color-mix(in oklch, black 8%, transparent), 0 28px 70px -24px color-mix(in oklch, black 30%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: A surface that has left the page: menu, popover, select, dialog, sheet. Kept in both themes.

shadows.name: ring-focus
shadows.purpose: The focus bloom on a control that takes one, beside the document-level 2px arc outline.

shadows.name: shadow-primary
shadows.purpose: One hair of weight under a primary button. Flattened to a single stop.

shadows.name: shadow-on-mesh
shadows.purpose: The same, on a dark ground.

shadows.name: shadow-modal
shadows.value: 0 2px 6px color-mix(in oklch, black 6%, transparent), 0 28px 70px -24px color-mix(in oklch, black 26%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Translation-layer shadow still named by the ported auth and admin screens.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: The default: anything arriving or changing state. Also the stylesheet's default transition curve.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: A longer arrival, crossing a meaningful distance: the plate unroll and the line draw.

motion.name: ease-mesh
motion.purpose: Ambient only — the plate's scanning rule and the orb drift. Symmetrical because it never arrives.

motion.name: duration-instant
motion.purpose: A tap, immediate feedback. Table row colour changes.

motion.name: duration-quick
motion.purpose: A hover or a state shift on something already on screen. The stylesheet's default duration.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: The default for anything entering or leaving; the plate unroll.

motion.name: duration-slow
motion.purpose: An enter animation; the line draw.

motion.name: duration-scan
motion.purpose: The rule travelling down a plate's drafting grid.

motion.name: popup-transition
motion.value: 150ms ease-out-quart on opacity, scale 0.98→1, 4px translate, origin var(--transform-origin)
motion.purpose: Every anchored surface opens and closes on this one string, as an interruptible state transition rather than a keyframe.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: The stylesheet's reduced-motion block; authored motion components also gate on useReducedMotion and keep the end state visible.

patterns.name: pattern-grid
patterns.purpose: The drafting grid a plate (and the daylight board) is drawn on. Plate grounds only, never the canvas.

patterns.name: pattern-hatch
patterns.purpose: The mark's three offset squares, filling a cell that has nothing to say.

breakpoints.name: table-scroll
breakpoints.purpose: Below this a wide table slides as one piece under a stationary frame instead of reflowing.

narrative.overview:
The cyanotype: the plan drawn in white on blue before anything is built. The console is a drawing board, not a dashboard. A proposal the product is still deciding about is drawn as a plate — abyss ground, chalk line work, a 32px drafting grid, a title block at the foot — and once it becomes a record it moves onto paper, where it is read as rows. That is the whole personality: the blue is where the product is proposing, the paper is where the operator is working.

The system's one aesthetic commitment is that the canvas is colourless. The ink ramp is achromatic — chroma exactly zero, both themes — so the only chromatic thing in a product surface is the brand hue, Royal Azure at hue 270. Everything interactive is that hue and nothing decorative is. The second commitment is that separation is a surface change: glacier → mist → paper is the layering, panels are flat, and a hairline is reserved for a data boundary. Both themes ship as equals, under the same token names.

Density is where it earns it. A table runs 32px heads, 36px rows, 12px gutters and 13px type; a plate breathes. The type scale is fixed pixels at a ~1.15 ratio, eleven steps, because an operator reads this at one DPI all day and a clamp() heading that shrinks inside a panel is worse, not better.
keyCharacteristics: One hue (Royal Azure, 270) on an achromatic ground; chroma 0 everywhere else in product surfaces.
Flat by default: surfaces separate, shadows are for things that have left the page.
Filled, not outlined: a secondary button and an input are the same well.
Fixed pixel type ramp, eleven steps, each carrying its own line-height and tracking.
Sentence case, no uppercase micro-labels, no second face except the figure.
Motion is a transition between two states, decelerating, and always gated on reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Hue Rule
rules.body: Product surfaces carry exactly one chromatic family: hue 270. The ink ramp is chroma 0 in both themes, so a coloured grey anywhere is a defect, not a choice.

rules.name: The Arc Is State Rule
rules.body: The arc family is interactive state and the brand. It is never decoration: no arc-tinted section backgrounds, no arc borders for emphasis, no arc icon that is not a control.

rules.name: The Three Inks Rule
rules.body: Only ink, ink-2 and ink-3 carry text. ink-4 and ink-5 are marks — gridlines, ticks, disabled glyphs — and putting a word in them fails the contrast the product commits to.

rules.name: The Pinned Field Rule
rules.body: A field that is an identity (arc, abyss, person-1…6) holds its value in both themes, and the ink on it is pinned (mesh-ink, person-ink) rather than inherited.

rules.name: The Word With The Colour Rule
rules.body: A status is a signal ink on its own signal tint and a word. Colour is never the only signal.

rules.name: The No Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is a claim that the characters are data. Figures line up because they are tabular-nums on the sans — set globally on td, th, output, time, data — not because they wear a typewriter. The console ships zero font-mono in markup and the stylesheet defines no --font-mono, so the utility cannot be reached for.

rules.name: The Two Places Rule
rules.body: The display face is allowed on the monumental figure and on plate numbers. Nowhere else; a second face without a job costs a token and buys nothing.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Sentence case everywhere — headings, buttons, column labels, nav, status pills. No uppercase eyebrows, no track-spaced micro labels, no kickers.

rules.name: The Scale Or Nothing Rule
rules.body: Eleven steps and nothing between them. A half-pixel size (text-[12.5px]) is a value nudged until one screen looked right.

rules.name: The Field Stops Rule
rules.body: Two adjacent regions are told apart by their surfaces meeting, not by a line between them. If two regions share a surface and need to be distinguished, one of them is in the wrong place.

rules.name: The One Row Rule
rules.body: A list screen spends one row before the data: title, trail, meta, actions. No eyebrow, no standing description, no KPI strip. Anything true to say on first run is said in the table's empty state.

rules.name: The Flat Panel Rule
rules.body: A panel is a surface and an edge. If it needs a drop shadow to be found, it is on the wrong ground.

rules.name: The Nested Panel Rule
rules.body: A panel inside a panel drops its ground and its shadow and keeps only its padding — enforced off the DOM in Card, so the double-framed box fails quietly instead of shipping.

dos: Do take every value from packages/tokens/src/tokens.ts. It is the only place a colour, radius, type step, easing or duration is written down; the stylesheet, the brand kit and the Figma exporter all read it.
Do separate regions with a surface change: glacier → mist → paper.
Do keep a hairline for data boundaries only — a table row, an input, a group break in the rail.
Do fill, don't outline: a secondary button is the same well as an input.
Do ask for a type role (text-sm, text-lg), which carries its own line-height and tracking.
Do spend arc on state — focus, selection, active, link — and arc-ink when the brand has to be text.
Do write sentence case, and let weight and colour carry hierarchy rather than size.
Do line figures up with tabular-nums on the sans.
Do gate every animation on useReducedMotion (or the stylesheet's reduced-motion block) and make sure the end state is what shows when motion is off.
Do use one named motion token: out-quart for state, out-expo for an arrival, 80/160/240/420ms.
donts: Don't use font-mono or declare a mono face. Figures are tabular, not typewritten.
Don't put a border on a section, a card or a page header.
Don't write an arbitrary type or tracking value (text-[12.5px], tracking-[-0.01em]); if a step is missing, the scale is what changes.
Don't reach outside the radius ladder (rounded-2xl and up), and don't put a rounded-* class on utilities that already decide radius — the caller names it once.
Don't put text on sky, powder, ink-4 or ink-5.
Don't use arc as decoration: no arc-washed sections, no brand-coloured icon that is not a control, no text-arc (use arc-ink).
Don't mark selection or the active state with a ring, an outline or a left border. The field takes the colour.
Don't stack atmosphere. One mesh per page at most, and only where the brand actually speaks; the plate's scanning rule is the product's single piece of ambient motion.
Don't add an eyebrow, a kicker or a standing description above a heading, and don't add a second explanatory row to a list screen.
Don't use a Lucide glyph in a grey disc as an empty state; name a kind and let the drawn mark do it.
Don't reach for a shadcn slot name (bg-card, border-border) in new work. The slots exist so vendored primitives resolve; authored surfaces name the token.
notCanonized: The command palette's shortcut hint still sets font-mono (packages/ui/src/components/command.tsx:158) — recorded as drift, not as a rule, and the No Mono Rule stands.
apps/console/src/components/common/data-table.tsx is the legacy table, still used by two supplier routes, drawing border border-border on bg-card. It is not the table this system documents.

The console's not-yet-redrawn surfaces (auth, onboarding, marketplace, _admin/_aff/_supplier, several app-shell popups) carry arbitrary type and tracking values and section borders. Ported fidelity, not house style.
